IncidentBot: :rotating_light: SEV2 created — streaming endpoints showing tail latency spike and stalls. p95 for /v1/stream jumped from ~120ms -> ~1.1s, p99 to ~4.3s since 2026-03-15T04:12Z. Symptoms: long gaps between SSE chunks / websocket heartbeats, client reconnects. Affected: hosted region eu-west-1 and select customers (ACME corp, beta group). Paging SRE-Oncall.

SRE-Oncall: acknowledged. I'm on it — adding traces + rolling up relevant dashboards. @Karen are you able to join? Can someone paste recent deploys/infra changes?

Asha Patel: I see a config change rolled at 04:12 UTC to edge-proxy: "enable_windowed_throttle=true, write_window=64kb" as part of a perf tweak. Ops ticket 5421.

Ethan Ng: grabbing network metrics now. Quick summary from edge-proxy logs:

```
[04:11:58] proxy: connection 10.0.4.22 -> client 52.x write_buffer=0.004s
[04:12:06] proxy: connection 10.0.4.22 -> client 52.x write_buffer=3.2s (evicted)
[04:12:12] proxy: tokenbucket: window_miscalc delta=-4096
[04:12:18] proxy: stall detected: shoving to socket, queuing; backpressure=true
```

Support Engineer: customer ACME reporting streaming sessions pause mid-response and then deliver all remaining text in a burst. They filed a support ticket with a short clip.

SRE-Oncall: hypothesis: the new windowed throttle config causes the proxy to accumulate writes and flush in big bursts when clients cannot keep up (client backpressure + small write_window miscalculation). That explains large gaps between chunks and high p99. Immediate mitigation plan:
1) revert enable_windowed_throttle at edge-proxy fleet (rollback to previous config)
2) deploy a temporary keepalive/heartbeat shim at edge to send zero-byte frames every 250ms for active streams
3) route heavy customers to dedicated streaming nodes (if available)
4) notify support -> ask ACME to switch to non-streaming fallback if they see client issues

Karen Miller: I'll take rollback. Rolling config revert to staging then prod. ETA ~6m. Posting command.

Karen Miller: `./ops/rollout_config --service=edge-proxy --flag=enable_windowed_throttle --set=false --batch=20` -> started

IncidentBot: deploy-bot: rollout started for edge-proxy config revert (batches 1/5).

Ethan Ng: while rollback runs, toggling edge-proxy keepalive. Command:
```
kubectl -n edge patch configmap proxy-conn --patch '{"data":{"streaming_keepalive_ms":"250"}}'
```

Asha Patel: keepalive patch applied to batch-1.

Support Engineer: Notifying ACME that we're working on it and providing a temporary polling fallback. cc: @ACME-SRE

Karen Miller: rollback batch-2/5 done, batch-3/5 -> ok. Watching latency graphs.

SRE-Oncall: observed immediate improvement on a subset of routes. p95 for those nodes dropped back to ~200ms, p99 ~480ms. Still seeing a few straggling nodes with bursts.

Ethan Ng: collecting tcp metrics — retransmit rate increased briefly, but KCPS and socket queues decreasing after rollback.

Asha Patel: found related log pattern: `tokenbucket: window_miscalc` — sounds like integer truncation for small windows coupled with upstream chunk coalescing. Might be a bug in how we compute available tokens when client window < chunk size.

SRE-Oncall: tactical follow-ups:
- Keep the rollback in prod and pause any further rollouts of windowed_throttle.
- Open bug for tokenbucket calculation, assign to eng-runtime.
- Post-mortem owner: Karen Miller.
- Notify product & account execs for ACME.

Karen Miller: created BUG-7839: "proxy tokenbucket miscalc with small write_window -> streaming stalls" and assigned to eng-runtime. Also created PM ticket for customer communication.

Support Engineer: ACME confirms streams are stable and they're no longer seeing mid-response pauses. They provided logs matching the earlier time window.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: metrics check: p95 (global streaming) now 180ms, p99 430ms. Error rate unchanged. Rolling window revert completed (5/5 batches). Monitoring set for 30m.

SRE-Oncall: handoff summary for next shift (from @SRE-Oncall -> @Karen Miller):
- What happened: edge-proxy windowed throttle config interacted badly with small-client windows, causing buffer accumulation and burst flushes that manifest as SSE/WebSocket chunk gaps and high p99.
- Impact: ~6-9% of streaming sessions in eu-west-1 experienced >2s gaps; ACME and a few beta customers affected.
- Mitigations implemented: config revert, keepalive shim, route shift for heavy customers, support notified.
- Outstanding: root cause fix in BUG-7839 + test coverage for write_window edge cases; run a canary to validate tokenbucket math at small window sizes.

Karen Miller: taking the on-call handoff for the next 8 hours. I'll coordinate with eng-runtime on bug and schedule a targeted canary. If anything regresses ping @SRE-Oncall or escalate to SEV1 if client reconnect rate spikes >2x baseline.

Asha Patel: posting quick diagnostic snippet for postmortem:
```
# approximate reproduction steps
1) set proxy write_window to 32k and enable_windowed_throttle=true
2) simulate slow-client consuming 1kb/s
3) observe tokenbucket available calculation and chunk flush events
```

Support Engineer: customer comms drafted. Will send out formal incident update to ACME and customers in affected orgs after we confirm stable for 30m.

SRE-Oncall: leaving the channel; will be available on pager if needed. Thanks everyone.

IncidentBot: SEV2 -> monitoring state: stable; next auto-check in 15m. If p99 rises above 2s, incident re-open will auto-trigger.
